records.comments: Canadian domestic student. Applied in early March; notified by the end of March. Also note: "The University of Western Ontario" is also known as "Western University." Additional notes: I already went to graduate school here (finished with an MSc in Industrial-Organizational Psychology in the past). I completed some additional coursework (enough to warrant a second bachelor's degree in Math) and this is what the 3.60 (standardized GPA that takes into account institution) is based on. My grade average (as calculated by the school) was an 84%, somehow (I'm not sure how they arrived at this number; I think that even including only my last two years would have resulted in an average of 83.5% so maybe they rounded?). Every course on this transcript was a math, statistics, or computer science course (only one course from computer science; everything else was a roughly even split of math or statistics). I also had three summer research internships in Math and Statistics. I did not include any GRE scores because I did not include these in my application, but if anyone's curious, my old scores (back when I got into grad school the first time) were 94th percentile analytical writing, 97th percentile verbal, and 89th percentile quantitative (and I think that's because during that year, if you got perfect, it would still only be 94th percentile because of how many people would get perfect on that section). I also had prior experience with my selected supervisor (i.e., I attended his class and worked with him for one of my summer research internships).

records.comments: Warning to future international applicants: I looked up all current MA students in the Communication Studies program at University of Nebraska-Lincoln and every single one is a U.S. citizen—and they all hold GTA (Graduate Teaching Assistant) funding offers. Unless you are gullible enough to waste $50, A word is enough for the wise.
